newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan overseas investment up by 39.1 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan overseas investment up by 39.1 pct in 1996.

text.p: Overseas direct investment by Japanese manufacturing companies is expected to grow by 39.1 percent in fiscal 1996 from the year-earlier period, the Export-Import Bank of Japan said on Friday.
Investment during this period, from April 1, 1996, to March 31, 1997, is estimated to reach about 1.35 trillion yen, the bank said.

The survey, which covered 321 manufacturers, showed that investments by Japanese electrical and electronic, chemical and automobile industries were the driving force behind the increase, with the primary regional focus on Asia.
Among the countries considered most promising for investment over the next three years or so, China tops the list, followed by Thailand and Indonesia, the bank said.

The ratio of overseas production is expected to follow a steady upward trend in the future, although it will not necessarily lead to a decline in exports or a large expansion of exports to Japan from Japanese overseas affiliates.

The recent yen depreciation has not affected overseas investment plans significantly, though the trend has helped improve international competitiveness for an increasing number of them, the bank added.
